hero.title1: AI agents your team can message.
hero.sub: PeopleFree.work builds AI agents that work through the channels your team already uses: email, texts, WhatsApp, Telegram, Signal, Slack, calendars, documents, and line-of-business tools.
hero.subBold: They handle the background busy work so people can focus on judgment, relationships, creativity, and strategy.

perks.sectionSub: Concrete help in the channels your team already uses, backed by careful human engineering.

wage.title: Absorbs the background work
wage.desc: Agents coordinate follow-ups, drafts, reports, reminders, and exception lists so people are not buried in operational noise.

iq.title: Strong AI, carefully engineered
iq.desc: We pair capable AI agents with experienced human engineers who shape the workflow around your real tools and constraints.

lang.title: Works across channels and languages
lang.desc: Email, texts, WhatsApp, Telegram, Signal, Slack, Teams, documents, and multilingual work can be part of one operating layer.

balance.title: People focus where people matter
balance.desc: Your team keeps judgment, relationships, taste, creativity, and strategy while the agent handles coordination and preparation.

benefits.title: Always watching the background
benefits.desc: The agent can monitor approved inboxes, calendars, reports, and shared folders so quiet problems surface before they become fire drills.

overtime.title: Follow-ups stop slipping
overtime.desc: Promised replies, missing documents, overdue invoices, and stalled approvals stay visible until a person closes the loop.

own.title: Built around your operation
own.desc: Your dedicated AI teammate learns your workflows, review rules, voice, source systems, and escalation boundaries over time.

ip.title: Your work stays yours
ip.desc: Documents, strategies, designs, reports, and creative work produced for your business belong to you under the agreed engagement.

dailyLayer.sectionTitle: A Daily Operating Layer Your Team Can Message
dailyLayer.sectionSub: Onboarding connects your agent to the email, calendar, documents, reports, texts, and chat channels your business already runs on. From then on, people can ask from normal tools and get a short list of what needs attention.
dailyLayer.flowOutput: Ask from Telegram, WhatsApp, Signal, email, or text. Get a reviewed action list.

briefing.title: Briefings in the channel you check
briefing.desc: A morning email, Telegram note, or WhatsApp message can summarize what changed, what is due, who is waiting, and what needs a decision.

triage.title: Email and text triage
triage.desc: Sorts messages by urgency, attaches context, and separates routine drafts from anything that needs a person’s judgment.

followUps.title: Follow-up tracking
followUps.desc: Keeps a live list of who owes what across inboxes, texts, shared docs, and reports. Quiet threads do not quietly disappear.

drafts.title: Draft replies for approval
drafts.desc: Writes first drafts in the right thread and waits for review when the message is external, sensitive, or outside the approved rules.

workflows.title: Workflow-specific work
workflows.desc: Once the daily basics are trusted, the same agent can take on billing prep, supplier chasing, listing follow-ups, content calendars, PR reviews, or deadline checks.

signals.title: Signal monitoring
signals.desc: Watches recurring reports, spreadsheets, connected apps, and operational feeds, then tells you which numbers moved or stopped arriving.

review.title: External messages can wait for approval
review.desc: The agent prepares the reply, explains the context, and leaves the send decision with the right person.

escalate.title: Unclear work comes back to a person
escalate.desc: Sensitive issues, missing inputs, and work outside the agreed scope are escalated instead of guessed.

team.sectionSub: Dedicated AI agents, engineered for specific workflows and supervised by your review rules.

search.reveal: Can’t find the workflow you need? We design custom agents around your tools, communication channels, approvals, and the work your team actually wants off its plate.
search.emailBody:
Hi PeopleFreeWork team,

I'm looking for an AI agent that can help with:

[Describe the role, tasks, or skillset you need]

olivia.title: Creative Director (AI Agent)
olivia.bio: An AI agent who prepares brand strategy, copy, and campaign drafts so creative people can spend more time on taste, direction, and original ideas.

devon.title: Senior Software Developer (AI Agent)
devon.bio: An AI agent who reviews pull requests, gathers CI context, drafts release notes, and prepares deployment checklists for engineers to approve.

sarah.title: Executive Assistant (AI Agent)
sarah.bio: An AI agent who manages calendars, triages emails, prepares meeting briefs, and keeps the next decision visible.

marcus.title: Legal Operations Specialist (AI Agent)
marcus.bio: An AI agent who tracks cases, prepares billing records, watches deadlines, and drafts routine legal operations work for review.

priya.title: Real Estate Coordinator (AI Agent)

james.title: Operations Manager (AI Agent)

sofia.title: Marketing Strategist (AI Agent)

elena.title: Bookkeeper (AI Agent)

yuki.title: Asia-Pacific Liaison (AI Agent)
yuki.bio: An AI agent who helps bridge cross-border communication, drafts multilingual updates, and keeps regional context organized.

aisha.title: Client Relations Manager (AI Agent)

examples.sectionSub: Concrete workflows where an agent works through email, texts, chat, documents, and approved tools while people stay in control.

emailMgmt.title: Multi-Account Email Management
emailMgmt.desc: Monitors multiple email accounts, flags urgent messages, includes full content in alerts, and tracks threads awaiting response across accounts.
emailMgmt.real: A litigation attorney's AI triages three inboxes and flags client emails needing reply within hours.

voiceBilling.title: Voice-to-Billing
voiceBilling.desc: Dictate time entries and billing notes by voice. Your AI transcribes, structures, and logs them automatically.
voiceBilling.real: A litigation attorney dictates billing entries via voice message. The AI transcribes and structures them into billable records automatically.

legalResearch.title: Legal Research & Drafting
legalResearch.desc: Integrates with legal databases, drafts memos, researches case law, and prepares zoning reports on demand.
legalResearch.real: An AI assistant researches case law databases, drafts zoning memos, and writes litigation expense summaries for attorney review.

dailyBriefings.title: Daily Operational Briefings
dailyBriefings.desc: Receive morning, midday, and evening email briefings covering your inbox, calendar, and system health.
dailyBriefings.real: A manufacturing executive receives 3 daily briefings covering unread emails, calendar events, and production system health.

contentWriting.title: Content Writing & Publishing
contentWriting.desc: Writes SEO-optimized articles, manages content calendars, and publishes directly to your website.
contentWriting.real: An AI content specialist writes and publishes luxury lifestyle articles with proper bylines and SEO optimization.

corpTax.title: Corporate Tax & Accounting
corpTax.desc: Files tax returns, generates invoices, categorizes expenses, and tracks corporate obligations.
corpTax.real: An accounting operations agent prepared T4A and T5 support plus a T2 return packet for human review at a small business.

codeReview.title: Code Review & Deployment
codeReview.desc: Reviews pull requests, generates architecture diagrams, posts inline review comments, and manages CI/CD.
codeReview.real: An AI engineer fetches GitHub PRs, generates architecture diagrams, and posts targeted inline review comments.

hourTracking.title: Client Hour Tracking
hourTracking.desc: Logs billable hours automatically, rotates tracking sheets when hours are exhausted, and alerts when budgets run low.
hourTracking.real: An AI assistant tracks client hours in shared spreadsheets with automatic tab rotation and budget alerts.

infraMonitor.title: Infrastructure Monitoring
infraMonitor.desc: Monitors servers 24/7 with self-healing: detects failures, attempts automated repair, and escalates only when needed.
infraMonitor.real: An AI ops engineer runs heartbeat checks across multiple server instances, self-heals broken services, and manages encrypted backups.

docProcessing.title: Document Processing
docProcessing.desc: Reads handwritten documents, proofreads emails, processes invoices, and extracts data from PDFs.
docProcessing.real: An AI assistant transcribes an attorney's handwritten notes into typed text and proofreads outgoing client emails.

morningBriefings.title: Multilingual Morning Briefings
morningBriefings.desc: Wake up to a personalized audio briefing in your language covering news, calendar, weather, and health metrics.
morningBriefings.real: A busy parent receives daily audio briefings in two languages covering world news, calendar events, and sleep data from their smart ring.

familyHealth.title: Family Health Tracking
familyHealth.desc: Integrates with wearables and health apps, tracks checkups, vaccination schedules, and health milestones for the whole family.
familyHealth.real: An AI assistant syncs smart ring data, workout stats, and tracks the kids' eye exam schedules and vaccination dates.

financialMonitor.title: Financial Monitoring
financialMonitor.desc: Tracks bank balances, monitors transactions, and alerts your family group when accounts run low.
financialMonitor.real: An AI monitors the family bank account and alerts the group chat if the balance drops below a set threshold.

smartShopping.title: Smart Shopping
smartShopping.desc: Checks your purchase history before recommending products, cross-references Reddit and Amazon reviews, and finds the best local prices.
smartShopping.real: Before suggesting a product, the AI checks past order history, then searches Reddit, social media, and local retailer reviews.

familyCoord.title: Family Group Coordination
familyCoord.desc: Monitors family group chats, auto-creates calendar events from conversations, and forwards school alerts.
familyCoord.real: When someone mentions dinner plans in the family group chat, the AI automatically creates a calendar event.

kidsEducation.title: Kids Education Planning
kidsEducation.desc: Maintains living knowledge files for each child tracking school decisions, activities, and milestone achievements.
kidsEducation.real: An AI assistant tracks each child's health assessments, extracurricular research, and activity schedules in living documents.

storybooks.title: Custom Children's Storybooks
storybooks.desc: Writes personalized stories, generates AI illustrations for each page, and compiles them into printable PDFs.
storybooks.real: An AI created a 15-page illustrated storybook with custom art for each page, compiled into a print-ready PDF.

petCare.title: Pet Care Management
petCare.desc: Tracks vet visits, vaccination schedules, weight, and dental care with proactive reminders.
petCare.real: An AI maintains vet records for two cats, tracks vaccinations, and flagged dental needs after a routine checkup.

travelPlan.title: Travel Planning
travelPlan.desc: Researches multi-city itineraries, monitors flight prices, and compares accommodation options.
travelPlan.real: An AI planned a 14-day multi-city family trip, tracking direct flights and price alerts under budget.

smartReminders.title: Smart Reminders with Escalation
smartReminders.desc: Sets reminders that start gentle and ramp up urgency as deadlines approach. Knows when to nudge and when to stay quiet.
smartReminders.real: Reminders follow the deadline and stop when the task is complete.

manufacturing.heroSub: A dedicated AI operations agent that monitors inboxes, ERP, sales, inventory, receivables, shipments, reports, and team channels so leadership sees the business clearly every day.

heroProof.label: executive briefings when you want them
sales, inventory, AR, backlog, and shortage reports

overview.title: Not a chatbot. A manufacturing analyst that keeps watch.
overview.body: Most manufacturers already have the data. It is scattered across email, ERP tables, spreadsheets, customer threads, supplier notes, calendars, and tribal knowledge. The agent sits across those systems, turns raw activity into operational judgment, and hands leaders the reports, summaries, and follow-up drafts they need before the day gets away from them.

items.title: Executive inbox layer
items.desc: Monitors priority contacts, flags urgent threads, drafts replies, preserves real email threading, and separates informational messages from items that need action.

items.title: ERP reporting analyst
items.desc: Queries order, invoice, inventory, customer, product, backlog, AR, and shipment data using reporting rules agreed with your team.

items.title: Dashboard builder
items.desc: Turns analysis into interactive HTML reports with KPI cards, trend tables, notes, source CSVs, and shareable links.

items.title: Ops reliability monitor
items.desc: Checks report delivery, link health, backups, security posture, and integration health so the reporting system itself stays trustworthy.

problems.title: Manufacturing leaders are drowning in fragmented signals
items: The answer to a simple executive question often spans email, ERP, calendar, spreadsheets, customer history, and yesterday’s operational context. Senior people spend their morning reconstructing the picture instead of deciding what to do.

Customer concentration, quote movement, backlog risk, shortages, overdue receivables, margin shifts, and shipment timing are visible in the data, but only after someone has time to pull and reconcile the data manually.

Reports are often trapped in one-off spreadsheets. The logic changes by person, the source data is not easy to inspect, and leadership cannot tell whether a number came from live ERP, a manual export, or a stale worksheet.

Business partners ask for updates, pricing comparisons, customer summaries, investor data-room support, or product analysis. The team can answer, but every answer steals focus from sales, production, and customer work.

solutions.title: What the manufacturing agent can own

items.title: Inbox monitoring and response support
items.desc: Watches priority inboxes, summarizes high-value threads, drafts replies, attaches reports, and keeps a clear audit trail of what it acted on and what it ignored.

items.title: Daily executive briefings
items.desc: Produces morning, midday, and evening updates covering calendar, inbox, sales pulse, shipments, collections, inventory, shortages, FX, weather, and relevant market news.

items.title: ERP and SYSPRO-style BI
items.desc: Runs governed reports across sales, backlog, AR aging, inventory, customer concentration, product movement, shortage exposure, and historical comparisons.

items.title: Customer and pricing analysis
items.desc: Builds customer-specific reporting, price comparison packs, product-line views, margin change summaries, and follow-up-ready executive notes.

items.title: Inventory and operational alerts
items.desc: Highlights critical stock, slow-moving inventory, material risk, replenishment issues, and shipment exceptions before they become fire drills.

items.title: Reliability and security checks
items.desc: Runs daily checks for uptime, backups, disk, memory, public ports, permissions, delivery health, and report-link verification.

operatingSystem.title: A practical operating system for the back office
operatingSystem.sub: The agent is strongest where manufacturing work crosses systems and functions.

items.label: Sales
items.title: Sales pulse and customer movement
items.desc: Tracks trailing sales, top customers, customer concentration, order changes, quote movement, and account-level follow-up opportunities.

items.label: Finance
items.title: Receivables and collections visibility

items.label: Operations

items.label: Pricing

items.desc: Compares products, customers, periods, and price movement with source tables and clear assumptions rather than unexplained spreadsheet math.

items.label: Leadership
items.title: Briefings that connect the dots
items.desc: Combines email, calendar, ERP, operational notes, and external context into plain-English updates with specific next actions.

items.label: IT/Ops
items.title: Delivery infrastructure that can be trusted
items.desc: Verifies dashboards, links, attachments, backups, and service health before leadership relies on the output.

examples.title: The work it can take off your team

items.title: Executive request answered with a report pack
items.desc: A partner asks for a customer/product comparison over the last 12 months. Normally that means pulling ERP exports, cleaning rows, building a spreadsheet, writing a summary, and sending attachments.
items.real: The agent generates an executive summary, an interactive dashboard, supporting CSVs, and a source-aware narrative. It can reply in-thread with the report link and attachments after approval or under agreed operating rules.

items.title: Morning briefing that replaces inbox digging
items.desc: A manufacturing leader starts the day with unread emails, meetings, shipment issues, sales questions, collection risks, and inventory warnings scattered across systems.
items.real: The agent sends a concise briefing: what changed, what is urgent, who is waiting, which accounts need attention, which inventory items are critical, and which reports are ready to inspect.

items.title: Receivables report that runs every week
items.desc: A finance team spends hours sorting aging buckets, checking last contact, asking sales for context, and preparing the same report again next Monday.
items.real: The agent produces the AR view on schedule, highlights accounts that crossed thresholds, adds last-touch context where available, and keeps the exportable data beside the written summary.

items.title: Customer risk and concentration surfaced early
items.desc: A few large accounts can quietly drive most revenue, backlog, or receivables exposure. When one slows down, the signal is often scattered across order history and email.
items.real: The agent tracks concentration and movement over time, flags unusual drops or spikes, and prepares customer-specific summaries that leaders can use for sales, investor, or partner conversations.

items.title: Inventory pressure made visible
items.desc: Shortages, slow movers, and critical counts are easy to miss when reports live in ERP screens that only a few people know how to read.
items.real: The agent converts those signals into a ranked operations list: critical stock, likely shortages, stale inventory, shipment blockers, and recommended follow-up owners.

items.title: Report delivery hardened
items.desc: A dashboard link is only useful if it opens, renders, and includes the right files when the executive clicks it.
items.real: The agent checks the report link, browser rendering, attachments, and expiry before delivery. If something fails, it fixes the delivery path before claiming the report is ready.

items.title: Reliability logs
items.desc: Health checks for report servers, backups, public links, permissions, and scheduled jobs.

directAccess.kicker: Ask from the floor, office, or road
directAccess.title: Talk to the manufacturing agent from Teams, WhatsApp, email, or Telegram
directAccess.sub: Leaders can request reports, approve drafts, and check exceptions without opening a new dashboard. The agent brings ERP, inbox, shipment, and receivables context back into the channel where the question started.
directAccess.note: Channels can include Telegram, WhatsApp, Signal, email, Slack, Microsoft Teams, or a private web chat, depending on your security policy and approval rules.

messages.text: What changed overnight? Give me the short version before the production meeting.
Three items need attention: two priority customer emails, one shipment now at risk for Friday, and 11 inventory items below reorder threshold. I marked assumptions where ERP data was stale.
Build a 12-month customer and product comparison for the top accounts. Include CSVs and a shareable dashboard.
Done. I generated the dashboard, attached the CSV packet, checked the link, and drafted a plain-English summary for approval.

controls.title: Human judgment stays in charge
controls.sub: Manufacturing teams need useful automation, not risky autonomy. The agent can be configured around your approval rules, data access boundaries, and delivery standards.

items.title: Approval gates for outbound communication
items.desc: Use review-first mode for new contacts, sensitive replies, pricing conversations, or anything that should remain human-approved.

items.title: Source-aware reporting
items.desc: Reports can include the source tables, time window, filters, and business rules used so leaders know where numbers came from.

items.title: No guessing when data is incomplete
items.desc: If a report has missing inputs, stale exports, conflicting records, or unavailable systems, the agent says so and marks the result as partial.

items.title: Secure deployment posture
items.desc: Access is scoped to approved systems, delivery links can expire, and operational checks watch for public exposure, stale credentials, and failed backups.

problems.title: What gets lost between channels
items: A client texts one team member while another holds the email thread. Staff spend time reconstructing the conversation before they can answer.
New inquiries, appointment changes, and pending documents arrive throughout the day. Without one owner and one list, follow-ups slip.
Generic automation can send a message without the right history or authority. A brokerage needs reviewable drafts and clear access boundaries.

overview.body: Leads arrive in one inbox, clients reply by text, showing details live on a calendar, and the next step hides in a document. A dedicated agent can connect those approved sources and prepare the work for the right person to review.

items.title: Shared inbox clarity
items.desc: Sort inquiries, requests, and updates into a short action list with the source conversation attached.

items.title: Text with context
items.desc: When a dedicated line is connected, bring replies into the same follow-up view as email. Group texting is tested with your carrier before rollout.

items.title: Appointments and handoffs
items.desc: Track who owns the next step, what was promised, and when the office needs to respond.

items.title: Documents ready for review
items.desc: Organize the details staff need for listing packets, client updates, and recurring office work.

directAccess.kicker: Texts become a controlled action list
directAccess.title: The real estate agent can triage multiple incoming texts at once
directAccess.sub: When buyers, sellers, agents, and staff text at the same time, the agent ties each message back to the right email thread, calendar event, and client record, then drafts replies for review.
directAccess.note: SMS/MMS, WhatsApp, email, and calendar access are configured around your approved line, carrier, and brokerage review rules.
directAccess.status: Monitoring approved text and email channels

messages.text: Can we move the 4:30 showing to 5:15? Also is the garage heated?
Any feedback from yesterday’s showing?
Offer package just came in. Who needs to review first?

I matched all three to their records. Drafted the buyer scheduling reply, found the garage note in the listing file, prepared a seller update, and marked the offer package for broker approval before anyone sends.

content.heroSub: A content operations agent that turns WhatsApp ideas, email approvals, research, calendars, CMS tasks, and drafts into review-ready work while creatives keep the voice and judgment.

items.title: SEO-Optimized Writing
items.desc: Articles, blog posts, and landing pages written with keyword research, proper heading structure, and meta descriptions baked in.

items.title: Content Calendar Management
items.desc: Plan, schedule, and track your content pipeline, with blockers surfaced early for the right person to resolve.

items.title: Brand Voice Consistency
items.desc: Your AI learns your brand's tone, style, and vocabulary. Every piece sounds like it came from your best writer.

items.title: Multi-Platform Publishing
items.desc: Write once, publish everywhere. Automatic formatting for WordPress, Medium, LinkedIn, and social media platforms.

items.title: Research & Fact-Checking
items.desc: Every claim verified, every stat sourced. Your AI researches topics thoroughly before writing a single word.

items.title: Image & Media Management
items.desc: Source stock images, generate AI visuals, optimize file sizes, and attach proper alt text for accessibility and SEO.

steps.title: Share your channels and voice
steps.desc: Tell us where ideas arrive, where approvals happen, and what makes the brand sound right.

steps.title: We build the workflow
steps.desc: The agent learns your calendar, CMS, research standards, approval rules, and channel preferences.

steps.title: Draft, review, publish

cta.title: Give your content team a steadier operating layer.
cta.sub: Let the agent carry research, drafts, calendars, and follow-ups so people can focus on voice and ideas.

examples.title: Content workflows that fit the team

items.title: WhatsApp idea to publishable brief
items.desc: A founder drops a rough campaign idea in WhatsApp between meetings.
items.real: The agent turns it into a content brief, checks the calendar, drafts posts for review, and keeps the final voice decisions with the team.

items.title: Editorial calendar that follows up
items.desc: Drafts, approvals, images, and publishing dates live in different tools.
items.real: The agent watches email, CMS, and calendar, then nudges the right person when a draft, quote, or approval is blocking publication.

items.title: Research pack before writing
items.desc: Writers need sources, examples, and audience context before the first draft.
items.real: The agent gathers source links, summarizes claims, and prepares a fact-checked outline instead of asking a person to start from a blank page.

directAccess.kicker: Creative work stays in the flow
directAccess.title: Message the content agent from WhatsApp, email, or your calendar
directAccess.sub: Drop an idea, request a brief, approve a draft, or ask what is blocking publication from the tools the team already checks every day.
directAccess.note: Channels can include WhatsApp, Telegram, email, CMS comments, shared docs, calendar, or Slack.

messages.text: Turn my voice note into a launch post and check whether Thursday conflicts with the newsletter.
I prepared the post, found a newsletter conflict Thursday, suggested a Friday slot, and added three source links for the claims.
Who is blocking next week’s articles?
Two drafts need quote approval, one image is missing alt text, and one topic needs a human decision on tone.

software.heroSub: An engineering operations agent that works through Slack, GitHub, email, CI, and monitoring tools to prepare reviews, incident context, release notes, and checklists for engineers.

solutions.title: What your engineering agent can prepare

items.title: Code Review & PR Management
items.desc: Fetches open PRs, generates architecture diagrams, posts inline review comments, and flags potential issues before they reach production.

items.title: Self-Healing Infrastructure
items.desc: 24/7 heartbeat monitoring across all servers. Detects failures, attempts automated repair, and only escalates what it can't fix.

items.title: CI/CD Pipeline Management
items.desc: Manages build pipelines, monitors deployment health, rolls back failed deployments, and tracks release history.

items.title: Documentation Generation
items.desc: Auto-generates API docs, architecture diagrams, runbooks, and onboarding guides from your codebase.

items.title: Bug Triage & Tracking
items.desc: Analyzes incoming bug reports, categorizes severity, assigns to the right team, and suggests potential fixes from similar past issues.

items.title: On-call context and escalation support
items.desc: The agent gathers alert context, drafts recovery checklists, and escalates the decisions engineers should make.

steps.title: Share your stack and channels
steps.desc: Tell us about GitHub, Slack, CI, monitoring, deployment, and the handoffs that waste engineering time.

steps.title: We connect the safe surfaces
steps.desc: The agent gets approved access, review rules, and escalation boundaries for incidents, PRs, and releases.

steps.title: Engineers decide, agents prepare
steps.desc: The agent gathers context and drafts updates while engineers keep architecture and production judgment.

cta.title: Give your engineers a calmer operations layer.
cta.sub: The agent can gather context, draft checklists, and watch systems while your team makes the important calls.

examples.title: Engineering workflows that keep humans in charge

items.title: Slack alert to reviewed fix plan
items.desc: An incident starts in Slack while logs, dashboards, and GitHub issues live elsewhere.
items.real: The agent gathers the error trail, links the likely commit, drafts the update, and asks an engineer before posting customer-facing status.

items.title: PR review without context hunting
items.desc: Reviewers lose time reconstructing architecture, test failures, and deployment risk.
items.real: The agent reads the PR, CI, and related issues, then leaves a review packet with suggested comments for an engineer to approve.

items.title: Release checklist that keeps moving
items.desc: Deployments depend on CI, migrations, docs, rollback notes, and stakeholder updates.
items.real: The agent tracks each step in Slack and GitHub, drafts release notes, and escalates only the decisions a human should make.

directAccess.title: Reach the engineering agent from Slack, GitHub, email, or pager alerts
directAccess.sub: The agent can gather logs, CI, PR context, and release status, then draft updates or checklists while engineers keep architecture and production judgment.
directAccess.note: Channels can include Slack, GitHub, email, PagerDuty-style alerts, Linear, Jira, or a private web chat.

messages.text: Why did checkout alerts spike after the deploy?
I linked the spike to release 2026.10.11, found two failing payment logs, and drafted a rollback checklist. I am waiting for your approval before posting status.
Can we ship the PR today?
CI is green, docs are updated, but the migration rollback note is missing. I drafted it for engineering review.

items.title: Invoice Generation & Tracking

items.title: Invoice follow-up with a human tone

items.real: The agent prepares email drafts with the last payment context and asks before anything sensitive is sent.

items.title: Deadline watch across tools
items.desc: Tax, payroll, HST/GST, and corporate deadlines sit across calendars, spreadsheets, and accounting software.
items.real: The agent sends a concise email or text reminder with what is ready, what is missing, and what needs accountant judgment.

directAccess.kicker: Books stay close to the conversation
directAccess.title: Send receipts, invoice questions, and deadline checks by email or text
directAccess.sub: The accounting agent prepares reconciliations, invoice follow-ups, and filing checklists, then asks for accountant approval where judgment matters.

messages.text: I just sent two receipts and a vendor invoice. Put them somewhere useful before I forget.
I extracted the details, suggested categories, matched one vendor to an open bill, and left all three entries waiting for accountant approval.
Which overdue invoices need a human follow-up today?
Four crossed the threshold. I drafted email follow-ups with last-payment context and held the sensitive account for your review.

serviceModel.title: Not a self-serve dashboard. A white-glove AI engineering partnership.

items.title: Designed around real work
items.desc: We start with the inboxes, texts, reports, calendars, and decisions your team already lives in, then shape the agent around that operating reality.
